doc: Dry-run + negative-test evidence for the Paper B depth-ladder step200000 eval driver.
gpu_cost: 0 GPU-h. No model was ever loaded; no eval process was started; the four training nodes were never touched. Every python invocation ran with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' or under DRY_RUN=1, which returns before the GPU section. nvidia-smi was queried read-only (--query-gpu / --query-compute-apps).

artifacts_under_test.synced_to_zwfy6: yes, via scp -O to .73; md5 verified identical on both disks

positive_controls.note: Assertions must PASS on real, known-good artifacts. If they failed here, they would be useless (an assertion that always fires is not an assertion).

ckpt_probe_real.cost: 5.6 s wall via torch.load(mmap=True) on a 34 GiB file; no weights materialised

battery_real_zwfy6_v2_reference_batterie.note: All 9 batteries of the clean single-protocol `_v2` set (the set PAPERB_FLIP_BOUNDARY_RESOLVED.md designates as the version of Table 4 to publish) pass unchanged. This is what pins the expected item counts.

driver_dryrun_wzc1_pass.cmd: DRY_RUN=1 ARM=keep8 CKPT=.../step121000.pt EXPECT_STEP=121000 NAME=7B_DRYRUN_keep8_probe CKPT_MD5_MODE=head SKIP_ARCH_GUARD=1 PROJECT_ROOT=<wzc1> bash scripts/eval_paperb_ladder_200k.sh
driver_dryrun_wzc1_pass.stopped_before: any GPU work; log line 'DRY_RUN=1 -> stopping before any GPU work. No model was loaded, no GPU touched.'

driver_dryrun_zwfy6_H20_pass_with_arch_g.cmd: DRY_RUN=1 ARM=keep12 PROJECT_ROOT=<zwfy6> PYTHON_BIN=/opt/conda/envs/torch-base/bin/python CKPT=outputs/olmo2_probe2_7B_keep12fresh2/step124000.pt EXPECT_STEP=124000 NAME=7B_DRYRUN_keep12_probe CKPT_MD5_MODE=head bash scripts/eval_paperb_ladder_200k.sh
driver_dryrun_zwfy6_H20_pass_with_arch_g.preflight: PASSED 8/8, arch guard NOT bypassed (cc 9.0 == REQUIRE_SM 9.0)
driver_dryrun_zwfy6_H20_pass_with_arch_g.significance: This is the exact invocation shape the real keep12 run will use, differing only in CKPT=step200000.pt / EXPECT_STEP=200000 / NAME / DRY_RUN=0.

negative_controls.note: Each row injects ONE deliberate defect and records the observed refusal. All 11 refused with rc=2 and a message naming the defect. None silently proceeded.

cases.injected: real keep8 ckpt at step121000, asserted with --expect-step 200000 (i.e. the exact mislabelling this driver exists to prevent)
cases.observed: ASSERT-FAIL: ckpt step is 121000, expected 200000: outputs/olmo2_probe2_7B_keep8fresh2/step121000.pt. Refusing to evaluate a non-endpoint checkpoint under a 200k label.

cases.injected: path outputs/olmo2_probe2_7B_keep8fresh2/step200000.pt (does not exist yet -- this is the real current state)
copied 6 of the 8 REAL keep14@200k shard files into a scratch dir and ran the harness's own --merge
cases.harness_behaviour_observed: the harness merged WITHOUT complaint and printed plausible numbers with n_nan=0 for all 6 tasks; arc_easy n=1782, which is byte-for-byte the historic keep12 defect (1782 = 6x297)
cases.observed_from_our_assertion: 13 DEFECTs listed, including 'n_shards=6 EXPECT 8' and 'arc_easy: n_scored=1782 EXPECT 2376 (=6.00/8 shards)'; then ASSERT-FAIL ... is INCOMPLETE (13 defects). Do NOT use these numbers.
cases.significance: Confirms empirically that eval_olmo2_probe2_downstream.py's merge() does NOT refuse a partial shard set, so the n_scored assertion is load-bearing and not redundant.

cases.injected: summary with full n=10042 for hellaswag but n_nan=3, n_scored=10039 (items dropped from the accuracy denominator while the item count looks right)
cases.observed: DEFECT: hellaswag: n_scored=10039 EXPECT 10042 (=8.00/8 shards) + DEFECT: hellaswag: n_nan=3 EXPECT 0 -> ASSERT-FAIL
cases.significance: This is the case a shard-file-count check alone would miss: 8/8 shard files present, merge clean, but 3 fewer items scored.

cases.observed: DEFECT: add_bos=True EXPECT False (Paper B base protocol: OLMo-2 gets no BOS) -> ASSERT-FAIL

cases.injected: openbookqa marked skipped with error 'HF 429 rate limit' (the real failure mode behind the historic keep12 partial merge)
cases.observed: DEFECT: openbookqa: SKIPPED (HF 429 rate limit) -> ASSERT-FAIL

cases.injected: PYTHON_BIN=<zwfy6>/olmo2_venv/bin/python on .73, which is a real symlink to /opt/conda/envs/elsa/bin/python = torch 2.7.0+cu126 -- the exact interpreter identified as the historic flip boundary
cases.observed: P0 torch=2.7.0+cu126 then FATAL: torch=2.7.0+cu126 but the clean single-protocol batteries are torch 2.13.x. A version change alone moves ~20 items (PAPERB_FLIP_BOUNDARY_RESOLVED.md). Use /opt/conda/envs/torch-base/bin/python.
cases.significance: Tested against the real offending interpreter, not a mock.

cases.injected: ran on LOCAL (compute_cap 10.0, B200) with the arch guard active
cases.observed: P4 compute_cap(s) on this node: 10.0, then FATAL: this node reports compute_cap=[10.0] but the ladder protocol requires 9.0 (H20) ... Run on .73/.82/.104, or set SKIP_ARCH_GUARD=1 AND record the deviation
cases.significance: This is the guard that keeps keep10's eval off the B200 it is TRAINING on. See protocol section 4.

cases.injected: NAME=7B_keep8_step121000_wzc1, which is a real published measurement directory on wzc1
cases.observed: FATAL: olmo2_ppl_results/7B_keep8_step121000_wzc1/summary.json already exists. Refusing to overwrite an existing measurement.

cases.injected: VAL=/tmp/_fake_val.npy (33554560 random bytes, same size as the real array)
cases.observed: P3 ... md5=fd9ef5ed3150c85d3d1a2c00afb32b4e then FATAL: held-out val array md5=... but every ladder PPL on record was measured on f2ea48a2074a2f38fc3b4477fceecf11 ... A different val array makes the PPL column non-comparable.
cases.significance: Size alone would not have caught this; the md5 pin does.

cases.observed: FATAL: unknown ARM=keep16 (expected keep8|keep10|keep12). To add a rung, extend this case and paperB/LADDER_200K_EVAL_PROTOCOL.md.

pinned_expected_counts.provenance: read 2026-08-15 from zwfy6:olmo2_downstream_results/7B_{keep8_step121000,keep10_step83500,keep12_step124000}_v2{,_know}/summary.json and zwfy6:olmo2_ppl_results/*_v2/summary.json. All three arms agree exactly, so these are the protocol's item inventory rather than one run's accident.

measured_etas_for_launch_ordering.method: delta(log timestamp) / delta(step) over the last 60 and last 200 logged step lines. NOT the tqdm/postfix s/step field, and not a single sample. Windows agree to <1%.
measured_etas_for_launch_ordering.note: keep10 arrives FIRST despite being furthest back in steps, because it is on a B200 at 1.34 s/step vs 5.9-7.9 s/step on H20. But keep10 must be evaluated on H20 (protocol section 4), and no H20 will be free until keep12 finishes -- see protocol section 7 for the resulting launch order.

cross_disk_transfer_measurement.method: scp -O of a 400 MiB random file from LOCAL(wzc1) to .73(zwfy6), timed twice
cross_disk_transfer_measurement.implication: a 39.0 GiB keep10 step200000.pt would take ~42-53 min single-stream. This is the cost of the protocol-mandated move of keep10's ckpt to zwfy6; it is acceptable (unlike the 45.4 GiB x2 / 42 h case recorded in CLAUDE.md for B-P0.4, which was rejected).
